description: The World Port Index (Pub. 150) is an online database of maritime port information published as a reference and navigational planning tool for mariners. For thousands of ports around the globe it gives the geographic location and more than 100 key characteristics and services, such as harbour size and type, shelter, entrance restrictions, channel, anchorage and cargo pier depths, maximum vessel size, pilotage, tugs, cranes, repairs, drydock and supplies. It is produced by the United States National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency, mainly from NGA Sailing Directions and charts and, where these are lacking, other authoritative sources; users can also propose new ports and updates through a crowdsource geoform. Coverage is worldwide at the level of individual ports. The complete content is a CSV file (UpdatedPub150.csv, the official version) updated monthly, and the WPI viewing application downloads CSV, GeoPackage, JSON, shapefile and file geodatabase; archived 2019 editions exist as PDF, Access and shapefile. It is free to download with no registration. Caveats: NGA states the index does not replace charts and detailed publications, depths are indicative, and crowdsourced additions vary in completeness. The WPI supplies port nodes and capacity attributes for maritime network flow, capacity planning and hazard exposure studies of ports, and complements the IMF PortWatch port activity data catalogued here.
